clue.text: Test case required by striker

parts.note: a Test, as in a Test match, is a match
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A trial lawsuit that a striking worker needs to bring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test case' reads as a legal phrase, but splits into Test (a cricket Test match) and case; the striker is a match, which needs the box it is struck on.
explanation.definitionFit: A match, the thing that strikes, needs the small container with a rough side to be lit.

clue.text: Club price appears steep

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A golf club's fees seem too high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like an adjective for the price, but it is the verb: to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To macerate is to soften by soaking, to steep in liquid.

clue.text: Moor's representative ?

parts.note: the actor who represents the Moor of Venice, Othello, on stage

explanation.surface: An agent for a North African.
explanation.walkthrough: The Moor is Othello; whoever plays him in Shakespeare's tragedy represents him.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragic actor plays roles such as Othello in serious drama.

clue.text: Greeting port official initially

parts.note: Hull is a port in Yorkshire

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of official

explanation.surface: A harbour official's welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is a port city on England's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hullo is a variant of hello, a greeting.

clue.text: Figure seen at Congo assembly

indicators.note: assembly means the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A dignitary is spotted at a gathering in the Congo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' rearranges AT CONGO.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-sided polygon is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Very funny cry ?

definitions.meaning: informally, a hilarious person or thing

explanation.surface: A shriek of laughter at something hilarious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hilarious is informally called this, and it is also a loud shrill yell.

clue.text: Sort of paper that appears best face up

parts.note: the cream is the best part

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means face's word reads from the bottom

parts.note: a dial is a face, as on a clock

explanation.surface: Writing paper that looks best right side up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face up' looks like an instruction for the paper, but it means DIAL read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream-laid is cream-coloured writing paper with a ribbed laid finish.

clue.text: Tree is the joiner, not West

indicators.note: not means the letter for West is removed

parts.note: a welder joins metal

explanation.surface: A carpenter is described as not from the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' suggests a carpenter, but it is the welder, who joins metals.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a small tree with white flowers and dark berries.

clue.text: Railway vehicle mounted by Latimer, for example

indicators.note: mounted means the pieces climb up the down light, read from the bottom

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A train carriage someone called Latimer climbed aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Hugh Latimer, a Protestant bishop, was burnt at the stake in Oxford in 1555.
explanation.definitionFit: Latimer died for his faith, so he is an example of someone killed for their beliefs.

clue.text: Rabelais' greatest characters

parts.note: read literally: the biggest figures in Rabelais are Gargantua and Pantagruel, huge beings

explanation.surface: The finest figures created by the French writer Rabelais.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greatest' suggests best, but Gargantua and Pantagruel are literally the largest.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargantua and Pantagruel are enormous beings of colossal size.

clue.text: About to take inexperienced novice as stroke

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
raw means green, inexperienced
L is the learner, a novice, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A coach takes on a beginner and teaches a swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: The front crawl is the freestyle swimming stroke.

clue.text: Last man in got fifty, apparently

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a low-order batsman who goes in near the end of the innings
fifty is L in Roman numerals, and the word tail ends in L, so its ender seems to have got fifty

explanation.surface: The final batsman made a half-century, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: a half-century is fifty runs, rarely scored by the weakest batsmen. The cryptic half reads the answer as 'tail ender': the last letter of TAIL is L, the Roman fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail-ender is one of the weak batsmen at the bottom of a cricket batting order.

clue.text: Musical instrument for gardener nothing new in that

indicators.note: new tells us these letters are made into something new, a fresh arrangement

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A musical instrument for a gardener, with nothing new in that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal: put O (nothing) with GARDENER and rearrange to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonium-type keyboard whose sound comes from vibrating metal tongues is a kind of musical instrument.

clue.text: Forbearance shown by Miss Pecksniff

definitions.meaning: one of the two daughters of Pecksniff in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit, sister of Charity

explanation.surface: Patience displayed by a Dickens character.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Pecksniff, the hypocrite in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit, has daughters named Charity and Mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Leniency or clemency is forbearance, and it is also the given name of one of Pecksniff's girls in Dickens.

clue.text: Opera character starting endless rioting

indicators.note: rioting suggests letters running wild, so they are rearranged
endless means the word starting loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A character in an opera sets off a riot that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts STARTING to STARTIN, and 'rioting' rearranges those letters into the Wagner hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristan is the hero of Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde.

clue.text: Article's about gold-It's, reread by speculators

indicators.note: about means the article and s go round the rest

parts.note: the definite article, the, with the s
or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: reread means the letters of it's are read in a new order

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about gold that speculators read again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reread' rearranges ITS to IST; THE+S goes 'about' OR+IST.
explanation.definitionFit: Theorists form hypotheses, speculating about how things work.

clue.text: Cabin gets sea air

definitions.meaning: a sailor's work song, an air sung at sea

explanation.surface: A seaside hut enjoys fresh sea breezes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sea air' looks like the breeze, but an air is a tune: the sailors' work song.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough hut is a shanty, and a sea shanty is a sailors' song.

clue.text: Sort of sketch that may need cutting?

definitions.meaning: a small quick drawing or brief description
a nail on the thumb grows and must be trimmed

explanation.surface: A drawing that may need editing down.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail sketch is a small rough drawing, and the nail on one's thumb needs trimming.

clue.text: Believe ancient deserts raised this plant

indicators.note: raised means the pieces are read upwards in this down light

parts.note: trow is an archaic word for believe
rats means deserts, abandons

explanation.surface: Trust that old desert lands produced this flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserts' looks like a noun for dry lands, but is the verb: to rat.
explanation.definitionFit: Starwort is a name for chickweeds and stitchworts, small herbs with star-shaped flowers.

clue.text: How the Queen and Albert treat metal

parts.note: Queen Anne, who reigned 1702 to 1714
Al is a short form of the name Albert

explanation.surface: A royal couple are shown at work in a metal foundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Queen and Albert' suggests Victoria and her husband, but the queen is Anne and Albert shortens to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat metal or glass and cool it slowly so it toughens is to temper it, a treatment of metal.

clue.text: Bubbles as feature film

parts.note: a froth of bubbles forms a film over a facial feature such as the chin when shaving

explanation.surface: A bubbly comedy released as a full-length movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature film' suggests cinema, but a feature is part of the face, coated with shaving foam.
explanation.definitionFit: Lather is soapy froth that coats the face when shaving.

clue.text: Our debt for -replacing fortification

indicators.note: read as re-placing, placing the letters again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone substitutes something to settle what we owe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' is read as re-placing: put the letters of OUR DEBT in new places.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a small outlying fort or stronghold, a kind of fortification.

clue.text: Rose, right easy-going type

parts.note: an ambler is someone who walks at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: Rose is the right sort for a relaxed person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a name or verb but is the flower; a rambler is a climbing rose.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is a type of vigorously climbing rose.

clue.text: Marsupial cut up 'night-flier

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means cut's word reads from the bottom

parts.note: mow means cut grass
a bat flies at night

explanation.surface: A pouched animal savaged a nocturnal flier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses MOW to WOM, then add BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The wombat is a burrowing Australian animal that carries its young in a pouch.

clue.text: This beast made Beatrix a non-starter

indicators.note: a non-starter loses its first letter, so the surname drops its opening letter

parts.note: Beatrix Potter, the children's author

explanation.surface: An animal caused the children's author to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: Beatrix Potter wrote animal tales; 'non-starter' takes the first letter from her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a river animal, a beast, and fittingly one Beatrix Potter wrote about.

clue.text: Archbishop, not fifty, in beautiful valley

indicators.note: not means fifty's letter is taken out

parts.note: William Temple, Archbishop of Canterbury, or his father Frederick
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A clergyman under fifty in a lovely vale.
explanation.walkthrough: Temple was the name of two Archbishops of Canterbury; take out L (Roman fifty).
explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Tempe in Thessaly was celebrated in antiquity for its beauty.

clue.text: Section of head lawyers once in London

parts.note: the temple is the flat part of the side of the head
the Bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: Part of the head of a law firm in old London.
explanation.walkthrough: Temple Bar was the gateway at the City of London's western edge, removed in 1878.
explanation.definitionFit: Temple Bar was a gateway that formerly stood on the boundary of the City of London.

clue.text: Schubert's music in this time ? -

parts.note: the operetta ... Time is set to Schubert's melodies, so this flower fills the gap

explanation.surface: A question about when Schubert's music was written.
explanation.walkthrough: Lilac Time is a 1922 English operetta adapted from Das Dreimäderlhaus, built on Schubert's tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrub with fragrant purple flowers gives its name to the Schubert operetta Lilac Time.

clue.text: Attacks underworld HQ? That's a shock

parts.note: bombs means attacks from the air
hell is the headquarters of the underworld

explanation.surface: Air raids on the gangsters' headquarters come as a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld' suggests crime bosses, but it is the realm of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombshell is a sudden shocking surprise.

clue.text: Plain-and backward on the whole

indicators.note: backward means on and its partner are read right to left together

parts.note: all means the whole

explanation.surface: A frank remark said all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns ON ALL around in one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad treeless grassy plain in South America.

clue.text: He believes he is motor-cycling, apparently

indicators.note: apparently means someone motor-cycling seems to be racing in the event, so the pair goes inside it

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man motor-cycle race
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man trusts he is out riding his motorbike, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a famous motor-cycle race; HE IS goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is someone who believes in God, one who holds faith.

clue.text: Ornament for tribe in belt form

indicators.note: in means tribe's word goes inside the other
form means the letters of belt are formed into a new shape

parts.note: a race is a people, a tribe

explanation.surface: A decoration for a tribe made in the shape of a belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges BELT to BLET, and 'in' puts RACE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is a decorative band worn round the wrist, an ornament.
